topic: Ind AS 33: Basic EPS with bonus issue
title: EPS with
simple_words: Bonus shares bring no new money, so restate old share counts as if the bonus came at the start.

definitions.meaning: Free issue of shares to existing holders, usually from reserves. Total resources do not change, only the share count.
Shares outstanding before the event are adjusted for the proportionate change, as if it occurred at the beginning of the earliest period presented.

key_points: Bonus shares are issued without consideration, so there is ==no time-weighting== of the bonus shares.
Basic EPS of current and !!all comparative periods is restated!! for the bonus.
Bonus after the reporting date but before approval of the financial statements: per-share figures use the new share count.
In that case, !!disclose that fact!! (Ind AS 33 and Ind AS 10).

formulas.name: Adjusted shares for pre-bonus shares
formulas.legend: O = old shares held before bonus; B = bonus shares. 1:1 bonus gives factor 2. Time-weight the pre-bonus shares as usual; do not weight B.

formulas.name: Basic EPS
formulas.legend: P = profit after tax less preference dividend (and tax on it): non-cumulative if declared, cumulative whether declared or not. W uses adjusted shares.

insight.punchline: Bonus reduces EPS per share, not value!
insight.text: Shares issued for cash after the bonus date are weighted normally and are not multiplied by the factor.

memory_trick.mnemonic: Cut the cake into more slices
memory_trick.explanation: A bonus cuts the same cake into more slices: more shares, same total. So restate every earlier period with the same number of slices.

steps: Find the bonus ratio and factor
exam_tip: Apply the factor only to shares outstanding before the bonus. Shares issued for cash after it are not multiplied.

doubt.question: Why not time-weight the bonus shares from the bonus date?
doubt.answer: No resources come in, so there is no extra earning capacity. Ind AS 33 treats the bonus as if it happened at the start of the earliest period.

mistakes_hook: don't let the factor run wild

mistakes.wrong: Time-weighting the bonus shares from the bonus date
mistakes.right: Bonus shares are not time-weighted; restate pre-bonus shares as if the bonus was at the start of the earliest period.

mistakes.wrong: Leaving the previous year's EPS unchanged
mistakes.right: Restate comparative EPS for the bonus, so that periods are comparable.

mistakes.wrong: Using profit before preference dividend as the numerator
mistakes.right: Deduct preference dividend (and tax on it): non-cumulative if declared, cumulative whether or not declared.

applicability: Ind AS 33 (basic EPS, para 64) and Ind AS 10
reviewer_note: No past-paper list was given, so past_papers is empty. Check that the para 64 reference matches the current Ind AS 33.
check_notes: Checker 1: Step 4 ('Bonus shares: outstanding from start') is wrong when shares were issued for cash during the year before the bonus. Under Ind AS 33 para 28, bonus shares on those cash shares count from the date the cash shares were issued, not from the start of the period. Correct version: 'Bonus shares rank from the same date as the shares they are issued on. For opening shares that is the start of the earliest period; for shares issued for cash before the bonus it is their issue date (the factor still applies).'

Checker 1: Key point 1 ('there is no time-weighting of the bonus shares') overstates the rule in the same way. Bonus shares have no time-weighting of their own from the bonus date, but they carry the time-weighting of the shares they were issued on. Correct version: 'Bonus shares are not weighted from the bonus date. Multiply the time-weighted pre-bonus shares by the bonus factor, so the bonus shares share the weighting of their parent shares.'
Checker 1: Insight punchline ('Bonus reduces EPS per share, not value!') is redundant wording, since EPS already means earnings per share. Better: 'A bonus reduces EPS, not value!' (wording only).
